first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous declines in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory_86 and memory_31 both demonstrate that onboarding simplification directly improves completion and activation—the core metrics now regressing. Verifying memory_86 (shortening onboarding improved completion rates) and memory_73 (promotional pricing effectiveness) will clarify whether the onboarding path degradation is addressable through simplification or if we should pivot to pricing defense. Simplify_onboarding targets root cause (declining completion rates) rather than symptom management. This preserves optionality: if verification reveals onboarding simplification is no longer effective, promotional_pricing remains available next cycle to defend against competitor. Standard_experiment scope allows measurement without over-committing resources during competitive pressure.

final.rationale: Verification confirms memory_86: onboarding simplification yielded +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% retention. This directly addresses the 4% QoQ completion decline and 6% activation regression. Verification also confirms memory_73's critical finding: promotional pricing drives acquisition (+31% signup, +18% revenue) but destroys long-term cohort quality (-12% retention, fails renewal). Given primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, promotional pricing is disqualified despite competitive pressure. The competitor's aggressive pricing is a short-term threat that will self-correct through cohort churn; our sustainable advantage lies in reducing friction and time-to-value. Simplify_onboarding replicates the proven +13% completion lift in current environment, counteracting QoQ regression while preserving retention quality and renewal economics. Standard_experiment scope enables rapid measurement and course correction if environment has materially shifted.
